boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Turlock-campus settings for quiet work, collaborative sessions, computer access, tutoring, and writing support.

cards.title: Start on Vasché’s First Floor
cards.subtitle: Library seating with workstations and wireless access
cards.notes: Bring a charged device and start on the first floor when you want library resources, computer access, and nearby research help.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library base for independent work and quick access to academic resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus-map page identifies a first floor in Vasché Library and says the library provides computer workstations, wireless internet, research help, and study seating.
cards.access_notes: Use during Vasché Library operating hours; consult the library before visiting because schedules can vary by term.

cards.title: Move Upstairs for a Study Session
cards.subtitle: Second-floor library environment near student support
cards.notes: Settle on the second floor for focused work, then use nearby Learning Commons services if an assignment needs another set of eyes.
cards.short_summary: An upper library floor that pairs study seating with nearby learning support.
cards.evidence_claim: The official map documents Vasché Library’s second floor, while the university identifies the Learning Commons in room L222 and study seating throughout the library.
cards.access_notes: Use during library hours; individual Learning Commons services may follow separate appointment and service schedules.

cards.title: Choose the Third Floor for Quieter Work
cards.subtitle: Upper-floor seating beside designated quiet and silent areas
cards.notes: Head to the third floor when your task needs fewer conversations, and follow posted quiet or silent-zone expectations once seated.
cards.short_summary: The library’s upper level is suited to concentration-heavy reading and drafting.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s official library strategic plan places designated quiet and silent study areas on the library’s third floor, near Special Collections and University Archives.
cards.access_notes: Observe the posted quiet or silent designation; access is limited to current library building hours.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for Group Work
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms distributed through the library
cards.notes: Book a group room before meeting, then bring the shared files or discussion prompts your team needs to use the reservation efficiently.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed reservable rooms give project teams a defined place to collaborate.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Vasché Library campus-map page states that reservable group study rooms are available throughout the library.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required for a specific group room; verify current availability and booking rules through the library.

cards.title: Use the Library Computer Labs
cards.subtitle: Technology-equipped work areas inside Vasché Library
cards.notes: Choose a computer-lab station when an assignment needs campus hardware, and save work to approved storage before ending the session.
cards.short_summary: Campus computers support coursework that is awkward to complete on a phone or personal device.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus-map page says Vasché Library contains state-of-the-art computer labs, and the reopening announcement documents modern computer areas.
cards.access_notes: Computer use is subject to university login, availability, technology-use rules, and current library hours.

cards.title: Work in the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Open study area in Vasché Library room L222
cards.notes: Bring the assignment you are actively working on and use the open tables before connecting with the appropriate academic-support service.
cards.short_summary: An open second-floor workspace anchors several forms of academic assistance.
cards.evidence_claim: The current official Learning Commons page locates the space at Vasché Library L222 and shows an open study area with tables, chairs, and a projection screen.
cards.access_notes: The office lists 8 a.m.–5 p.m. hours; tutoring, writing, evening, and weekend services follow schedules linked through StanTutor.

cards.title: Build a Session Around Tutoring
cards.subtitle: Learning Commons academic-support space
cards.notes: Check StanTutor for the relevant subject and service time, then arrive with course materials plus one or two specific questions to address.
cards.short_summary: A structured stop for studying alongside course-specific academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies the Tutoring Center as a Learning Commons service in Vasché Library L222 and directs students to StanTutor for service hours.
cards.access_notes: Check StanTutor for current in-person or online availability; service hours can differ from the Learning Commons office schedule.

cards.title: Bring a Draft to the Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Writing support within the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Arrive with a draft, prompt, or outline and identify the stage of writing where feedback would be most useful before the session begins.
cards.short_summary: A writing-focused setting for developing an assignment with guided feedback.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Learning Commons page lists the Writing Center among its services at Vasché Library L222 and notes in-person and online availability.
cards.access_notes: Consult StanTutor or the Writing Center schedule before arriving; daytime, evening, weekend, in-person, and online availability may differ.

cards.title: Study Between Stops in the Student Center
cards.subtitle: First-floor study space near campus services and dining
cards.notes: Use the first floor for a shorter work block between commitments, keeping headphones handy because the building also supports dining and events.
cards.short_summary: A central, multipurpose option for coursework between other campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus-map page documents the University Student Center’s first floor and states that the building provides several study and conference spaces.
cards.access_notes: Current fall and spring building hours are Monday–Thursday 7:30 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday 2–8 p.m.; Saturday closed.

cards.title: Try the Student Center’s Upper Level
cards.subtitle: Second-floor space in the central campus hub
cards.notes: Go upstairs when you want an alternative to the library, then choose seating that does not conflict with a reserved conference space or event.
cards.short_summary: An upper-level alternative for informal individual or collaborative coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus-map page documents the University Student Center’s second floor and confirms that the building contains several study and conference spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use open common seating during posted Student Center hours; conference spaces may be unavailable when reserved for meetings or events.
